terms: Viewport ka sabse bada image/text block kab render hua. Target ≤ 2.5s.
LCP = server response + resource discover + download + render delay ka sum.
fetchpriority="high" se browser LCP image ko pehle fetch karta hai.
t0_0.what:
Definition: Largest Contentful Paint batata hai ki user ko page ka mukhya content kitni jaldi dikha — aksar hero image ya bada heading. Good: ≤2.5s, poor: >4s (75th percentile par).

LCP 4 hisson mein toot-ta hai: TTFB, resource load delay, resource load duration, element render delay. Pehle dekho kaun sa hissa bada hai.
t0_0.why: Ye user ke 'page load ho gaya' feel ka sabse close metric hai aur SEO ranking signal bhi. Galat jagah optimize karne se (jaise image compress, jabki problem late discovery hai) kuch nahi badalta.
t0_0.code: // field mein measure import { onLCP } from 'web-vitals'; onLCP(({ value, entries }) => send({ lcp: value, el: entries.at(-1).element?.tagName }));
where: hero image ya heading LCP hota hai.
Search Console Core Web Vitals report.
pros: Direct user-perceived load speed se connected
cons: Server, network aur render teeno par depend — root cause dhoondhna padta hai
gotchas: LCP image par loading="lazy" lagana sabse common galti
CSS background image ko browser late discover karta hai — <img> ya preload use karo
Client-side rendered app mein LCP JS ke baad hi aata hai

terms: Page ke saare interactions mein se lagbhag sabse dheema (p98) interaction latency. Target ≤ 200ms.
Main thread par 50ms se zyada ka kaam — input handle hone se rokta hai.
INP ke teen phases: handler se pehle wait, handler ka time, aur next paint tak.
t0_1.what: Definition: Interaction to Next Paint click/tap/keypress ke baad screen update hone tak ka time measure karta hai. 2024 mein FID ki jagah aaya kyunki FID sirf pehla interaction aur sirf delay dekhta tha.
t0_1.why: Main thread busy ho (bada JS, hydration, heavy re-render) to button click ke baad UI atakta hai. INP kharab hone par site 'laggy' lagti hai chahe load fast ho.
cons: Lab mein reproduce karna mushkil; field data (RUM) chahiye
gotchas: Third-party scripts bhi main thread block karte hain
Chhoti handler bhi bade re-render ke wajah se slow ho sakti hai
INP page ke poore lifetime ke interactions dekhta hai, sirf load nahi

terms: Unexpected layout shifts ka cumulative score. Target ≤ 0.1.
Visible element ne bina user input ke jagah badli.
Image/ad/embed ke liye pehle se width, height ya aspect-ratio dena.
t0_2.what:
Definition: CLS impact fraction × distance fraction se banta hai. User click ke 500ms ke andar hone wale shifts count nahi hote (expected hain).

Common causes: dimensions ke bina images, late-loading ads/banners, font swap, dynamically inject hua content upar.
t0_2.why: Button dabate waqt layout hil jaye to galat cheez click ho jati hai. CLS user trust aur conversions dono par asar karta hai.
where: images aur ads ki jagah reserve karna.
pros: Fix aksar simple CSS/markup change hota hai
cons: Late dynamic content debug karna thoda tricky
gotchas: bfcache restore ke baad bhi shifts count ho sakte hain
Content upar insert karne ki jagah neeche ya reserved slot mein dalo
Font swap bhi CLS banata hai

terms: Pehla content pixel (text/image) kab dikha. Target ≤ 1.8s.
Head ka CSS/sync JS jab tak load na ho paint ruka rehta hai.
FCP kharab ho to LCP bhi kharab hoga.
t0_3.what: Definition: First Contentful Paint page par kuch bhi (non-white) dikhne ka pehla moment hai. Ye TTFB aur render-blocking resources par depend karta hai.
t0_3.why: User ko 'kuch ho raha hai' feedback chahiye. FCP jaldi ho to bounce kam hota hai, bhale hi poora content baad mein aaye.
t0_3.code:
<head>
  <style>/* chhota critical CSS inline */</style>
  <link rel="preload" href="/app.css" as="style" onload="this.rel='stylesheet'">
  <script src="/app.js" defer></script>
</head>

new PerformanceObserver((l) => {
  const fcp = l.getEntriesByName('first-contentful-paint')[0];
  console.log('FCP', fcp.startTime);
}).observe({ type: 'paint', buffered: true });
cons: Akela FCP user experience ki poori kahani nahi batata
gotchas: Blank white screen ke baad spinner bhi FCP count ho sakta hai
CSS jitna bada utna FCP late
Fonts invisible text FCP ko delay kar sakte hain

terms: Request bhejne se response ka pehla byte aane tak ka time. Target ≤ 800ms.
User ke paas ke server se serve karna taaki latency kam ho.
Server/CDN ne bina origin tak jaaye response diya.
t0_4.what: Definition: TTFB mein DNS, TCP/TLS, redirects aur server processing shamil hain. Ye baaki sab metrics ki baseline hai — TTFB 1.5s ho to LCP 2.5s mushkil hai.
t0_4.why: Frontend optimizations tab bhi kaam nahi aati agar HTML hi der se aaye. Slow DB queries, origin ka door hona, redirects aur cold starts sabse common kaaran hain.
pros: Har metric ko seedha behtar karta hai
cons: Backend/infra team ke saath coordinate karna padta hai
gotchas: Redirect chains TTFB badha dete hain (http→https→www)
Cache hit/miss alag TTFB dete hain — dono measure karo
Serverless cold starts spikes banate hain

terms: Controlled test (Lighthouse, DevTools) — reproducible par synthetic.
Asli users ka data (CrUX, web-vitals library) — realistic.
Chrome User Experience Report: public field data, 28-day rolling.
t0_5.what: Definition: Performance measure karne ke do tareeke: lab (Lighthouse, DevTools Performance panel) debugging ke liye aur field (CrUX, PageSpeed Insights, web-vitals JS library se RUM) asli user experience ke liye.
t0_5.why: Aapka laptop + fast WiFi aur user ka mid-range phone alag duniya hain. Lab se fix dhoondho, field se verify karo ki asli users ko fayda hua.
pros: Lab + field dono se poori tasveer
cons: Field data aane mein time lagta hai (28 din rolling)
gotchas: Lighthouse score aur CrUX alag aa sakte hain
Chrome DevTools mein CPU/network throttle karo
75th percentile target hota hai, average nahi

terms: State change, parent re-render, context value change.
Naye virtual tree ka purane se diff nikal ke minimal DOM update.
Object/function har render naya banta hai, isliye memo ke liye alag dikhta hai.
t1_0.what:
Definition: Component tab re-render hota hai jab uska state badle, parent re-render ho, ya jo context wo padhta hai wo badle. Re-render ka matlab function dobara chalana (render phase) — DOM update zaroori nahi.

Props same hone par bhi child default mein re-render hota hai jab parent render ho.
t1_0.why: Optimization se pehle mental model chahiye: 'render slow hai' ya 'bahut zyada renders ho rahe?' Zyada tar apps mein problem component ki state ko bahut upar rakhna hota hai.
cons: Concurrent features ke saath rendering semantics thode complex
gotchas: Re-render != DOM update — React diff karta hai
Context value badle to saare consumers re-render
Index as key ya inline objects se unnecessary work

terms: Component ko wrap karta hai: props shallow-equal hon to re-render skip.
Props ke top-level values Object.is se compare.
t1_1.what: Definition: memo(Component) render skip kar deta hai agar props pichle render jaise hi hain. Lekin har render par naya object/function bana kar pass karoge to props 'badle hue' maane jate hain aur memo bekar jata hai.
t1_1.why: Memo ka khud ka cost hai (comparison + memory). Sirf tab fayda jab component mehenga ho aur props aksar same rahen. React Compiler aane ke baad bahut jagah manual memo ki zarurat kam hoti hai.
where: Parent jo frequently re-render hota hai
cons: Comparison cost, code noise
gotchas: Inline {}, [], arrow functions props mein memo tod dete hain
Children prop (JSX) har baar naya object hai
Pehle profile karo, phir memo lagao

terms: Mehengi calculation ka result cache karta hai jab deps na badlein.
Function reference ko stable rakhta hai.
Jab ye badle tab hi value/function dobara banta hai.
t1_2.what: Definition: useMemo(() => compute(a, b), [a, b]) value ko cache karta hai; useCallback(fn, deps) function ko cache karta hai (useMemo(() => fn) jaisa). Dono ka maksad referential stability ya costly compute bachana hai.
t1_2.why: Ye free nahi hain: memory + dependency comparison. Zyada tar chhoti calculations ke liye overhead fayde se zyada hota hai. Sahi use: (1) memo wale child ko stable props dena, (2) hook dependency mein stable function chahiye, (3) sach mein mehengi calculation.
cons: Deps galat hone par stale values ke bugs
gotchas: useCallback akela kuch nahi karta agar child memo nahi hai
Deps array mein sab used values hone chahiye (lint follow karo)
Compiler on ho to manual memoization zyada tar hata sakte ho

terms: React DevTools tab jo commits ka time aur reason record karta hai.
Component tree ka render time visual / slowest-first list.
Props/state/hook ka kaun sa change render laaya.
t1_3.what: Definition: DevTools Profiler mein 'Record' dabake interaction karo; har commit ka flame chart dikhta hai. Grey = render nahi hua, rang = render hua (kitna time). Settings mein 'Record why each component rendered' on karo.
t1_3.why: Anumaan se optimize karna band karo: pehle profile, phir fix, phir dobara profile. Production profiling ke liye profiling build chahiye.
where: kaun sa component zyada render ho raha.
cons: Dev mode timings production se alag hote hain
gotchas: Production profile ke liye profiling build chahiye
StrictMode dev mein double render karta hai — confuse mat ho
Sirf render time nahi, commit/paint bhi dekho

terms: Sirf visible rows DOM mein render karna, baaki nahi.
Viewport ke thoda bahar extra rows render karna taaki scroll smooth lage.
Rows ki height alag ho to measure karna padta hai.
t1_4.what: Definition: 10,000 rows ki list mein sirf ~20 visible rows render hoti hain; scroll par rows reuse hoti hain. Libraries: react-window, @tanstack/react-virtual.
t1_4.why: DOM nodes bahut ho jayein to layout, paint aur memory sab slow ho jate hain. 100+ complex rows ke baad virtualization ka fayda dikhta hai.
cons: Ctrl+F, a11y, dynamic heights aur SEO mushkil
gotchas: Item key stable rakho, index nahi
Variable height ke liye measure aur cache chahiye
Print/Ctrl+F offscreen rows ko nahi dhoondh paata

terms: State update ko non-urgent mark karta hai; isPending deta hai.
Typing/click urgent; list filter ka heavy render transition.
Kisi value ka 'peeche chalne wala' version deta hai.
t1_5.what: Definition: startTransition(() => setState(...)) React ko batata hai ki ye update interrupt ho sakta hai. Urgent updates (input typing) pehle process hote hain aur heavy render peeche chalta hai, UI atakta nahi.
t1_5.why: Search box mein type karne par 10,000 items filter karne wala render input ko freeze kar deta tha. Transition ke saath input turant update hota hai aur list baad mein.
cons: Total work kam nahi hota, sirf prioritize hota hai
gotchas: Transition ke andar async/await ke baad ke updates track nahi hote (React 19 mein actions better)
Controlled input ka state urgent hi rakho
Heavy render ko memoize bhi karo, transition akela magic nahi

terms: Treemap jo dikhata hai kaun si library kitna JS add kar rahi hai.
Ek package ke multiple versions bundle mein.
Import hua par use nahi hua.
t2_0.what: Definition: rollup-plugin-visualizer, webpack-bundle-analyzer ya vite-bundle-visualizer se build output ka treemap milta hai. Bade rectangles = bada size. Pehle sabse bade hisse se shuru karo.
t2_0.why: Bundle size direct parse/execute time aur INP/LCP par asar karta hai. 'moment.js' ya poora lodash import jaisi galtiyan treemap mein turant dikhti hain.
where: heavy deps ki jagah halke alternatives.
cons: Stats gzip/brotli aur parsed size alag hote hain — dono dekho
gotchas: Sirf gzipped size nahi, parsed + execute time bhi matter
Duplicate versions (peer deps) ko dedupe karo
Source maps analyzer ko zyada accurate banate hain

terms: Bundle ko chhote chunks mein todna jo zarurat par load hon.
import('./x') — Promise return karta hai, chunk alag banta hai.
Component ko lazily load karke fallback dikhana.
t2_1.what: Definition: Route-based splitting sabse pehle karo (har page ka alag chunk). Phir heavy components (charts, editors, modals) ko interaction par load karo. Chunk prefetch se next navigation instant lagta hai.
t2_1.why: User ko pehle page ke liye poora app ka JS download nahi karna chahiye. Initial bundle chhota = FCP/LCP/INP behtar.
cons: Loading waterfalls aur spinners ka risk
gotchas: Bahut zyada chhote chunks network overhead badhate hain
Lazy component ko Suspense boundary chahiye
Prefetch on hover/idle se delay chhupao

terms: Bundler unused exports ko final bundle se hata deta hai.
Static import/export — analyze ho sakte hain; CommonJS require nahi.
package.json mein flag jo bataye module import-time side effect nahi karta.
t2_2.what: Definition: Bundler static ESM imports se dekhta hai kaun se exports use nahi hue aur unhe drop kar deta hai. CommonJS dynamic hota hai isliye shake nahi hota.
t2_2.why: Barrel files (index.ts jo sab re-export kare) aur side-effectful modules tree shaking tod dete hain; poori library bundle mein aa jati hai.
cons: Side effects ke wajah se bundler safe side par rehta hai
gotchas: CSS imports ko sideEffects mein list karo warna drop ho sakte hain
export * aur barrel files shaking rokte hain
Dev mode mein shaking nahi hoti — production build check karo

terms: Gzip se 15–25% chhota compression; text assets ke liye best.
Build time par .br/.gz banana, server sidha serve kare.
Fonts aur images ke modern compressed formats.
t2_3.what: Definition: Text assets (HTML/CSS/JS/JSON/SVG) ko Brotli (ya gzip) se compress karo. Static files ko build time par pre-compress karo (highest level); dynamic responses ko on-the-fly medium level par. Browser Accept-Encoding bhejta hai, server Content-Encoding se jawab deta hai.
t2_3.why: Network bytes seedha load time hain. Images/video ko compress karne ke liye compression headers kaam nahi aate — format hi badlo (AVIF/WebP).
cons: Max-level Brotli on-the-fly CPU-heavy hota hai
gotchas: Already compressed files (jpg/mp4/woff2) ko dobara compress mat karo
Vary: Accept-Encoding header zaroori hai CDN ke liye
Brotli sirf HTTPS par browsers use karte hain

terms: HTTP/2 mein ek connection par kai parallel requests.
preload = abhi chahiye (current page), prefetch = shayad agle page mein.
Third-party origin se connection pehle hi kholna.
t2_4.what: Definition: HTTP/2 multiplexing aur header compression se bahut saari chhoti files ka cost kam hota hai (HTTP/1.1 jaise 6-connection limit nahi). Server push deprecated hai; uski jagah 103 Early Hints aur resource hints use karo.
t2_4.why: Hints ko sahi jagah lagao: critical late-discovered resource ko preload, cross-origin API/CDN ko preconnect, agla page ko prefetch. Galat preload bandwidth chura leta hai.
t2_4.code:
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://cdn.example.com" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/inter.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="prefetch" href="/next-page.js">
<link rel="modulepreload" href="/chunk-a.js">

<!-- speculation rules: agla page prerender -->
<script type="speculationrules">{"prerender":[{"urls":["/pricing"]}]}</script>
cons: Zyada hints priority ko dilute karte hain
gotchas: Preload bina use ke console warning deta hai aur bandwidth waste
Font preload ko crossorigin chahiye
Preconnect sirf 2–3 critical origins par

terms: Browser/CDN ko batata hai kitni der cache karna hai.
app.3f9a.js kabhi nahi badalta — saal bhar cache.
Purana turant do, background mein refresh karo.
t2_5.what: Definition: Strategy: HTML par no-cache (har baar validate), hashed static assets par max-age=31536000, immutable, API/data par stale-while-revalidate. Content-hashed filenames se deploy par naya URL milta hai, cache invalidation ki zarurat nahi.
t2_5.why: Repeat visits par network bilkul avoid ho jata hai. Galat headers ya to stale site dikhate hain ya cache ka fayda gawa dete hain.
t2_5.code:
# HTML
Cache-Control: no-cache

# /assets/app.3f9a1c.js
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable

# API
Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300
ETag: "v42"

// service worker SWR
self.addEventListener('fetch', (e) => e.respondWith(
  caches.match(e.request).then((hit) => hit || fetch(e.request))
));
cons: Invalidation planning zaroori
gotchas: no-cache ka matlab 'cache mat karo' nahi, 'validate karke use karo'
HTML ko long cache mat do — naya deploy atak jata hai
no-store bfcache bhi rok sakta hai

terms: Best compression, JPEG se ~50% chhota; encode slow.
Visual match par quality ~60–80 aksar kaafi.
t3_0.what: Definition: Modern formats: AVIF < WebP < JPEG size mein. <picture> mein AVIF, phir WebP, last mein JPEG fallback do. Photos ke liye AVIF/WebP, logos/icons ke liye SVG.
t3_0.why: Images page ke bytes ka bada hissa hote hain aur LCP aksar image hota hai. Format badalna kai baar code optimize karne se bada win hota hai.
t3_0.code: # build npx sharp-cli -i hero.jpg -o hero.avif --format avif --quality 50 # ya image CDN: /hero.jpg?format=auto&w=800
cons: Encode time aur pipeline setup
gotchas: Screenshots/flat graphics ke liye PNG/WebP lossless better ho sakta hai
Bahut compress karne par artifacts dikhte hain
Image CDN se auto-format + resize aasan hai

terms: Layout mein image kitni wide dikhegi (browser iske hisaab se chunta hai).
t3_1.what: Definition: srcset + sizes browser ko viewport aur DPR ke hisaab se sahi image chunne dete hain. Art direction (mobile par alag crop) ke liye <picture> ke media source use hote hain.
t3_1.why: 1x laptop ko 3x phone ki image bhejna bandwidth ki barbadi hai; phone ko chhoti image bhejna blurry dikhta hai. Sahi sizes performance aur quality dono deta hai.
cons: Multiple variants generate karna (build/CDN)
gotchas: sizes galat ho to browser badi image uthata hai
Width/height do — CLS bachta hai
srcset mein x aur w descriptors mix mat karo

terms: Offscreen images/iframes ko tab load karo jab viewport ke paas aayein.
Image decode main thread block na kare.
Custom lazy loading ya infinite scroll ke liye.
t3_2.what: Definition: Below-the-fold images par loading="lazy" lagao; above-the-fold (khaas kar LCP) image par eager (default) + fetchpriority="high". decoding="async" decode ko main thread se hata deta hai.
t3_2.why: Initial page weight kam hota hai. Lekin LCP image ko lazy karne se LCP bahut kharab ho jata hai, ye sabse common perf bug hai.
t3_2.code: const io = new IntersectionObserver((es) => es.forEach((e) => { if (e.isIntersecting) { e.target.src = e.target.dataset.src; io.unobserve(e.target); } }), { rootMargin: '200px' });
cons: Scroll par late load flicker ho sakta hai
gotchas: LCP image par lazy mat lagao
Lazy images ko width/height chahiye (CLS)
Carousel ke next slides ko preload sochna padta hai

terms: Above-the-fold render ke liye minimum CSS jo head mein inline hota hai.
Page par use nahi hui rules — coverage tool se milti hain.
Baaki CSS ko non-blocking load karna.
t3_3.what: Definition: CSS render-blocking hai. Critical CSS inline karo, baaki ko media="print" onload trick ya preload se async load karo, aur DevTools Coverage / PurgeCSS se unused CSS hatao.
t3_3.why: Bada stylesheet FCP/LCP ko seedha delay karta hai. Framework ke saath tools (Next, Astro) kaafi kuch khud karte hain.
t3_3.code:
<style>/* inline critical: header, hero */</style>
<link rel="preload" href="/app.css" as="style" onload="this.onload=null;this.rel='stylesheet'">
<noscript><link rel="stylesheet" href="/app.css"></noscript>

// PurgeCSS / Tailwind JIT
content: ['./src/**/*.{js,tsx,html}']

# critical npm package
npx critical index.html --base dist --inline
cons: Critical CSS maintain karna aur FOUC ka risk
gotchas: Inline CSS cache nahi hota
Dynamic classes purge ho sakti hain — safelist do
@import chains waterfall banate hain

terms: Sirf zaroori characters rakhna (Latin) — file chhoti.
t3_4.what: Definition: Fonts ko woff2 mein serve karo, subset karo, critical font preload karo aur font-display: swap (ya optional) rakho. Variable font se kai weights ki jagah ek file.
t3_4.why: Fonts render-blocking text banate hain (FOIT) ya layout shift (FOUT swap). System font stack sabse tez option hai.
cons: Subsetting aur fallback tuning ka effort
gotchas: Preload mein crossorigin zaroori
swap CLS laata hai; metric-matched fallback use karo
Google Fonts self-host karna aksar faster hai

terms: MP4/WebM GIF se 5–10x chhota; GIF kabhi nahi.
Below-fold video ke bytes tab tak mat lo jab tak play na ho.
transform/opacity GPU par; layout/paint se bachte hain.
t3_5.what: Definition: Animated GIF ko <video autoplay muted loop playsinline> se replace karo. Below-fold video par preload="none" + poster. Animation sirf transform/opacity se karo.
t3_5.why: GIF bahut bhaari hota hai aur CPU heavy bhi. Video + poster se bytes kam aur playback smooth hota hai.
t3_5.code:
<video autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="none" poster="clip.avif" width="640" height="360">
  <source src="clip.webm" type="video/webm">
  <source src="clip.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

# GIF → MP4
ffmpeg -i in.gif -movflags faststart -pix_fmt yuv420p out.mp4

.card { transition: transform .2s; }  /* layout nahi */
cons: Autoplay policies (muted + playsinline chahiye)
gotchas: Autoplay sirf muted video ke saath chalta hai
Poster image dena mat bhoolo
will-change ko sab par mat lagao

terms: Metric ya size ka max limit jo build ko fail karwa deta hai.
t4_0.what: Definition: Budget = limit: 'main JS ≤ 170KB gz', 'LCP ≤ 2.5s', 'CLS ≤ 0.1'. CI mein check hota hai; budget tootne par PR fail ya warn karti hai.
t4_0.why: Performance dheere-dheere kharab hoti hai (har PR mein thoda JS). Budget regressions ko merge se pehle rokta hai, aur team ko shared target deta hai.
cons: Kaafi tight budgets team ko slow kar sakte hain
gotchas: Realistic (data-based) budgets rakho, aspirational nahi
Lab metrics noisy hote hain — multiple runs ka median
Budgets time ke saath review karo

terms: CI mein Lighthouse chalake results aur assertions.
Metric ka threshold; fail par build red.
t4_1.what: Definition: @lhci/cli se har PR par Lighthouse chalta hai, scores compare hote hain aur PR par comment aata hai. GitHub Actions mein treosh/lighthouse-ci-action aam hai.
t4_1.why: Manual Lighthouse bhoolna aasan hai. CI mein chalne se performance ek automated quality gate ban jata hai, bilkul tests ki tarah.
cons: CI machines ke variance se noisy results
gotchas: Number of runs badhao (3–5)
Test URLs representative aur stable rakho
Lab score field performance ki guarantee nahi

terms: Browser aur network ke beech ka proxy script (background mein chalta).
Fetch strategies — speed vs freshness trade-off.
t4_2.what: Definition: Service worker requests intercept karke cache se serve kar sakta hai. Strategies: cache-first (static assets), network-first (API/HTML), stale-while-revalidate (feed, avatars). Offline fallback page aur Background Sync (queued actions) bhi possible.
t4_2.why: Repeat visits instant, offline support aur PWA features milte hain. Lekin update/invalidation galat ho to users purana app dekhte rehte hain.
cons: Debugging aur update flow complex
gotchas: SW update par purane tabs purana version chalate hain — skipWaiting/prompt plan karo
Sirf HTTPS par (localhost exempt)
HTML ko cache-first mat karo bina versioning ke

terms: Server HTML par JS attach karke use interactive banana.
Sirf interactive widgets hydrate hote hain, baaki static HTML.
Qwik: hydration ki jagah serialized state se turant resume.
t4_3.what: Definition: Poore page ko hydrate karna heavy hai (TBT/INP kharab). Selective hydration (React Suspense), islands (Astro), aur resumability (Qwik) kam JS ke saath interactivity dete hain. Below-fold components ko idle/visible par hydrate karo.
t4_3.why: SSR HTML jaldi dikha deta hai par page tab tak 'dead' rehta hai jab tak hydrate na ho. Hydration cost kam karke INP aur TBT behtar hote hain.
cons: Architecture aur framework dependent
gotchas: Server/client HTML mismatch hydration errors deta hai
Islands ke beech state share karna mushkil
Prerender ≠ interactive; users ko fake-interactive UI dikhne se bachao

terms: Analytics, ads, chat widgets, tag managers — aapke control ke bahar.
Real embed ki jagah light placeholder (YouTube thumbnail) jo click par load ho.
Third-party scripts ko web worker mein chalana.
t4_4.what: Definition: Third-party scripts main thread, network aur CLS par asar daalti hain. Measure: Lighthouse 'reduce impact of third-party code', DevTools Network by domain. Fix: async/defer, lazy load, facades, Partytown, aur Tag Manager audit.
t4_4.why: Aksar site ka sabse bada slowdown aapka code nahi, tag manager ke andar chhupe 15 scripts hote hain. Unka asar bina measure kiye nahi dikhta.
t4_4.code:
<!-- facade: iframe click par -->
<lite-youtube videoid="abc123"></lite-youtube>
